The additions are pure observability + one return field; whether and how Fizeau evolves role/correlation-aware routing intelligence over time is a Fizeau-internal decision and is NOT specified here.\n\n## Background\n\nDDx today imports github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau (CONTRACT-003 at docs/helix/02-design/contracts/CONTRACT-003-ddx-agent-service.md). To implement Story 10's automatic escalation + reviewer pairing without DDx becoming a router (DDx must not pin Provider/Model — the spec calls that out as anti-pattern at line 374), DDx needs:\n\n1. To know the **power** of the model that was actually dispatched, so it can request 'next call must be at least one rung stronger' via MinPower without importing catalog code into DDx.\n2. To **tag** calls with what kind of work they're doing (Role) so Fizeau, telemetry consumers, and session log readers can distinguish implementer / reviewer / decomposer / etc.\n3. To **link** calls that share work context (CorrelationID — e.g., 'bead_123:attempt_4') so reviewer + implementer + retry attempts can be joined in logs and aggregations.\n\nDay 1 these are PURE observability — Fizeau's routing logic is unchanged. Future Fizeau evolution may use Role/CorrelationID for routing decisions; that's separate work, not specified by this contract change.\n\n## What changes\n\nExecuteRequest gains:\n- Role string — normalized: lowercased, alphanumeric+hyphen only, max 64 chars; reject invalid pre-dispatch with typed RoleNormalizationError. Empty = unset.\n- CorrelationID string — normalized: printable ASCII (no control chars, no whitespace except hyphen/colon/underscore), max 256 chars; reject invalid with typed CorrelationIDNormalizationError. Empty = unset.\n\nRouteRequest gains the same two fields with the same normalization (parity with Execute so ResolveRoute previews don't diverge).\n\nServiceRoutingActual gains:\n- Power int — catalog-projected power value (per § Catalog Power Projection at line 983) for the actually-dispatched Model. 0 means unknown/exact-pin-only when applicable.\n\nCONTRACT-003 reserved-cross-tool metadata keys list (today: produces_artifact, media_type) extends with:\n- role\n- correlation_id\nCollision behavior: top-level field wins; emit MetadataKeyCollision warning event when caller also sets Metadata['role'] or Metadata['correlation_id']. Future versions may reject duplicates.\n\nEcho behavior: Role + CorrelationID echoed into Final + RoutingDecision event.Metadata, plus session log header (one line per session). NOT echoed into per-event text_delta metadata to avoid per-token bloat (existing Metadata echo path on text_delta still applies for caller-supplied metadata that is NOT these reserved keys).\n\nSelection precedence (line 374) is UNCHANGED for Day 1. Role and CorrelationID are observational only; they do NOT enter the precedence chain. If a future change adds routing-affecting behavior keyed on these fields, the precedence section must be amended at that time.\n\nRouting Policy Test Contract (line 1448) gains minimum statements:\n- Role + CorrelationID are echoed into RoutingDecision + Final events\n- Role + CorrelationID are echoed into the session-log header\n- Role + CorrelationID are NOT echoed into text_delta event metadata\n- Role + CorrelationID never affect eligibility filtering Day 1\n- Without a CorrelationID, routing is unchanged from baseline\n- ResolveRoute and Execute observe identical routing policy for the same correlation-aware request (Day 1: both ignore for routing)\n- Invalid Role / CorrelationID values rejected pre-dispatch with the typed errors\n- ServiceRoutingActual.Power reflects the catalog-projected power of the dispatched Model\n- When caller sets both top-level Role and Metadata['role'], top-level wins and a MetadataKeyCollision warning is emitted\n\n## What this enables downstream (informational)\n\nDDx will use these fields to:\n- Compute next-attempt MinPower from previous.RoutingActual.Power + rung_step (cost-tier escalation)\n- Tag implementer + reviewer calls with Role for telemetry; share CorrelationID for trace-join\n- Set MinPower = implementer.RoutingActual.Power + 1 on the reviewer call (best-effort 'more powerful'); 'different provider' is best-effort emergent, not promised\n- When same-provider results on review, log a degradation event for operator visibility\n\nDDx will NOT:\n- Pin Provider/Model\n- Implement any tiebreaker keyed on CorrelationID\n- Define role-specific routing policy\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Role-specific Fizeau routing policy (config registry, per-role defaults, etc.)\n- Correlation-aware routing intelligence (tiebreakers, diversity bias, learned preferences)\n- Multi-tenant correlation namespacing\n- Cancellation semantics for any future correlation state\n- DDx→Fizeau outcome-feedback API\n- Anything keyed on Role or CorrelationID that affects routing\n\nIf Fizeau evolves any of the above, those are separate proposals with their own design docs (correlation-aware routing must specify state
